text: The attorney general of Guatemala (fiscal general de la República de Guatemala) serves as the chief public prosecutor and head of the Ministerio Público (Department of Justice). Under article 251 of the Constitution of Guatemala, the attorney general is appointed by the president from a group of six candidates who must be lawyers and possess the same qualifications as the magistrates of the Supreme Court. These candidates are nominated by a commission composed of the chief justice of the Supreme Court, the deans of the law schools at the country's universities, and both the chairman of the bar association and the chairman of its honor tribunal. The attorney general serves a four-year term and enjoys the same immunity as the magistrates of the Supreme Court. The president may remove the attorney general only if there is a justified reason, as specified in article 14 of the Organic Law of the Ministerio Público, which states that removal is permitted only in cases of conviction of the attorney general for committing a crime while carrying out their duties.
